chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which of the deeds is most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That you praise Him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved deed to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies praising Allah (hamd) as the most beloved deed, emphasizing that sincere gratitude is the essence of worship. This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that hamd is not merely verbal but a state of the heart that acknowledges divine favor, serving as the foundation for all other acts of devotion. It underscores the theological principle that recognizing God's blessings is the primary means of drawing closer to Him.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Husayn, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Which of the deeds is the most Beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Your praising Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following: “
Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘What deed is the most beloved to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy?’ The Imam said, ‘It is your deed of praising Him.’”
